title: 140 women had a severe outcome
plain_language: In four months at one hospital, 140 women either died (16) or nearly died (124) from pregnancy complications.
so_what: Near-misses vastly outnumber deaths, so they offer far more chances to learn what's going wrong.

title: About 1 in 9 didn’t survive
plain_language: The case fatality rate among severe-outcome women was 11.43% - 16 deaths among 140 critically ill women.
so_what: Once a woman is this sick, survival is far from certain; getting ahead of the crisis is what saves lives.

title: Eight near-misses for every death
plain_language: There were 7.75 maternal near-misses for every maternal death - 124 women survived a life-threatening complication.
so_what: Reviewing near-misses, not just deaths, gives a much richer picture of where care breaks down.

title: Bleeding and high blood pressure led
plain_language: Three quarters of severe cases came from direct causes; postpartum haemorrhage (17.9% of cases) and hypertensive disorders were the leading reasons.
so_what: These are exactly the emergencies basic obstetric care is meant to handle - readiness matters most here.

title: Anaemia and heart disease killed too
plain_language: Among the 16 deaths, severe anaemia and cardiovascular disease each accounted for about 19% - as many as the top direct causes.
so_what: Programmes focused only on obstetric emergencies can miss anaemia and heart disease.

title: Nearly half the babies fared badly
plain_language: About 45% of these pregnancies ended in a poor perinatal outcome, including 39 perinatal deaths.
so_what: A mother in crisis usually means a baby at risk; the two outcomes travel together.

title: Blood ran short when it mattered
plain_language: More than half the women (52%) needed a transfusion, and roughly 40% of them received too little blood.
so_what: A reliable blood supply is a basic, fixable gap standing between a near-miss and a death.

title: Team, protocol-based care saved lives
plain_language: Women who received prompt per-protocol management from a skilled team were far less likely to die (a strong protective effect in the analysis).
so_what: The fix isn’t exotic - it’s having trained staff follow the emergency protocols, every time.

title: Older mothers lost more babies
plain_language: Perinatal deaths were higher among mothers aged 20 and above, especially 35 and older, than among teenagers.
so_what: Age helps flag which high-risk pregnancies need the closest watch for the baby’s sake.
